subject.title: [优化建议] 添加结构化错误处理和智能重试机制

question: Should OpenClaw's installers actively classify and repair npm install failures, or should they remain diagnostic-only with manual recovery guidance?
rationale: The requested behavior changes setup UX and may mutate user npm configuration or retry global installs; source inspection shows a clear gap, but the safe default policy is a maintainer product decision.

options.title: Approve bounded classifier policy
options.body: Implement explicit transient retry and non-transient remediation branches in install.sh/install.ps1, with tests for network, EACCES, ENOSPC, EBADENGINE, E404, and Docker config-get behavior.

options.title: Diagnostics-only policy
options.body: Keep retries limited to the current cleanup/build-tool cases and improve printed guidance/docs without automatic permission repair beyond existing Linux prefix handling.

options.title: Defer installer policy
options.body: Leave the issue open as product backlog until maintainers decide whether installer automation may mutate npm/PATH state on macOS and Windows.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded classifier policy
recommendation.body: Implement explicit transient retry and non-transient remediation branches in install.sh/install.ps1, with tests for network, EACCES, ENOSPC, EBADENGINE, E404, and Docker config-get behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The history pass shows the strongest installer ownership signal and recent diagnostic/install verification changes on this surface.
